Bonsai 2 does some additional tuning in addition to just quantizing (mostly around the fp16 block weights per 32 params), so they’re able to pack more in to just so few GB.

The tradeoff with unsloth seems to be that it’s more directly applicable for other off the shelf open models, whereas with Bonsai you’d have to wait for them to release another one

3eb7988a1663 · Nov 14, 2026

As an experiment I took, not this current quant, of Qwen 3.8 27B and had it analyze some of my writing in CPU-only mode with llamacpp. Tried a Q4 and Q5. It was dreadfully slow, but you fire that off before bed, and you can get results the next day. This was a ~6000 word markdown file, took maybe 10 minutes before it started generating anything at all, but then it just cranks away. I would need to tune down the default thinking intensity, but it otherwise did the job.

Not compatible with vibe coding, but if you want a local tool to review content, it is possible today.

danielhanchen · Nov 14, 2026

Yes! One method is KV cache compression to 4-bits - llama.cpp does have hadamard, but it's not very accurate - we were researching if 4-bit KV cache can be used with a sliding window of 1024 for example of 8-bit KV cache

So we can have a 4bit KV cache, but the most recent N tokens can be 8bit - we found accuracy improves 2x!
